correctness.rationale: The Hessenberg condition for \(h=(3,4,4,4)\) is exactly \(SL\subset H\). Forgetting the intermediate plane gives a \(\mathbb P^1\)-bundle over the line-hyperplane incidence complete intersection \(\varphi(v)=\varphi(Sv)=0\). Linear dependence of the two differentials is equivalent to \((S-\mu I)v=0\) and \(\varphi(S-\mu I)=0\), which for the two two-dimensional eigenspaces produces exactly two \(\mathbb P^1\) singular components downstairs and hence two \(\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1\) components upstairs. An eigenbasis chart gives \(u+x=0\) and \(py+qz=0\); the quadratic form has rank four, so the transversal is a three-dimensional ordinary double point. The projective-line bundle adds one smooth coordinate. The local model also proves normality. The bundled symbolic checker verifies the local equations, Hessian rank, source-patch coordinate change, and eight fixed-point count.

originality.rationale: The exact 2017 source records the example's irreducibility, one patch equation, and eight singular torus-fixed points, but not the full singular locus. The later codimension-one theorem gives only a singular-locus containment for general semisimple operators, with equality reserved for nilpotent operators. Exact-object, local-normal-form, determinantal-cone, and quadric-stratum searches found no prior statement of the two disjoint quadric surfaces or the uniform transverse ordinary-double-point model. The 2024 Cummings thesis is a residual access risk because its abstract concerns semisimple patch radicality and the full text was unavailable.
residual_risks: The full 2024 Cummings thesis was not accessible, so an equivalent local computation hidden there cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: The exact example was introduced to show that a nonstandard semisimple Hessenberg variety can be irreducible and singular, but prior work records only patch/fixed-point evidence and later general work gives only semisimple containment. Identifying the entire singular locus as two smooth quadric surfaces and proving a uniform transverse ODP type converts that example into a complete structural description, explains the eight singular torus-fixed points as four on each component, and yields normality. This is a natural geometric invariant of a published benchmark example rather than an arbitrary slice or parameter substitution.
